bug_semantics: libnfs_zdr_string decodes an attacker-controlled uint32_t string length from a crafted NFS/RPC reply, then uses the mixed-width check `zdrs->pos + size > zdrs->size` (later `pos + (int)size`) as the only length gate before memcpy/in-place decode. ZDR.pos and ZDR.size are signed int; size is unsigned. A huge wire length wraps that addition so the bounds check passes, after which opaque copy or `buf[pos+size]` indexing runs past the receive buffer. The maxsize argument is unused. The 2026 fix rejects `size > zdrs->size` before the overflowing add.
flaw_origin: 763cd6e3e2bbb6906186e7ed6a86660276b596b7 (2012-07-04, "ZDR: New builtin replacement for RPC/XDR called ZDR") created lib/libnfs-zdr.c and first wrote libnfs_zdr_string with `if (zdrs->pos + size > zdrs->size) return FALSE;` and an unused maxsize. Parent 061d3f1f99e354af36e8ac259a98f863975e51f5 has no lib/libnfs-zdr.c and no zdr_string. Later dc8e10df only inserted an (int) cast for WIN32 warnings; 4476f11b and d1999dc9 changed decode allocation, not the missing size validation.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: a crafted NFS server can send a string size that overflows the signed pos+size bounds check, so decode proceeds past the buffer. That check and unused maxsize were born with ZDR in 763cd6e3 (2012); parent tree lacks the file, so this is the smallest public first-write. The WIN32 (int) cast and later decode-allocation edits are not the origin. Fix 55c18ea is the first content change that rejects size > zdrs->size and matches the advisory.
